original_question: If a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of CP^n has infinitely many periodic orbits, must those periodic orbits satisfy the quadratic growth bound lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2?
target_in_paper: Problem 3 in the section by Bernhard Albach, Umberto Hryniewicz, and Alexandru Oancea: the CP^n test case of the broader quadratic-growth question for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the specific ambient manifold CP^n, the hypothesis that the Hamiltonian diffeomorphism has infinitely many periodic orbits, and the intended quadratic lower-growth inequality from the paper’s Problem 3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: The paper’s counting function must be defined: for each T, P(T) is the number of periodic orbits of period at most T. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
Only primitive periodic orbits are counted; iterates of lower-period orbits are not counted separately. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The paper phrases this as a test case of the broader Problem 1, so the sharpened question should explicitly ask whether the counting function satisfies the same inequality, not whether the orbits themselves somehow 'satisfy' it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify the symplectic structure on CP^n relative to which 'Hamiltonian diffeomorphism' is meant.
refined_question: Let phi be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of complex projective space CP^n, equipped with its standard symplectic structure, and for each T > 0 let P(T) denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of phi of period at most T (so iterates are not counted separately). If phi has infinitely many periodic orbits, must one have lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 3, not the broader Problem 1: the paper first introduces the general quadratic-growth question for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms, then immediately lists two test cases, of which CP^n is the second. The nearby introductory paragraph also supplies the hidden notation your draft omits, namely that P(T) counts periodic orbits of period at most T and that only primitive periodic orbits are counted. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1)) The paragraph following Problem 3 explains why CP^n is singled out: Shelukhin’s theorem already covers complex projective spaces but yields only a weaker prime-like lower bound, so the paper’s actual open problem is whether the full quadratic bound holds in this case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
